subject: Intermittent 429s due to token-burst quota mismatch — recovery plan
messages:

Cc: infra@cyberloom.ai

Subject: Re: Sporadic 429 errors - spike at 09:00 PT

Attached is a short CSV showing request times and endpoints. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Matt

From: aditya.rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, grace.oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sporadic 429 errors - spike at 09:00 PT

Quick tech summary from infra: we collected traces and correlated them to a quota translation mismatch between two layers of the control plane. The tenant-level "burst_tokens" setting was being shadowed by an older per-application default policy during a config refresh at ~08:58 PT, which lowered allowable concurrent token bursts for short-lived high-token requests.

What happened:
- CybeRloom's ingestion sends periodic high-token bursts (500-800 tokens per request) that normally fit within the tenant burst profile.
- During a config sync we failed to reconcile the app-level default with the tenant override due to a race in the config-merger path (race condition reproducer in JIRA-INF-5712).
- For ~17 minutes the effective burst ceiling was lower, causing rate limiter to emit 429s for the high-token requests.

Actions taken so far:
- Rolled back the config refresh across the affected hosts (09:10 PT).
- Applied a targeted override to restore the tenant burst profile (09:12 PT).
- Collected full request traces and exported them (request-trace-20261001.zip).

Next steps we recommend for you:
1) Retry with exponential backoff where possible (looks like you already have this).
2) If you can, stagger large-batch ingestion by a minute during our remediation window.

We will publish a postmortem doc and the fix for the config-merger race. I'll coordinate with Olga on timeline and credits for impacted requests.

- Aditya
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Harris <matt.harris@cyberloom.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, infra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Customer recovery plan + timeline (CybeRloom)

Hi Matt — summary + concrete customer-facing plan: 

Root cause (short): a config-merge race caused tenant-level burst_tokens to be temporarily overridden by an older app default during a control-plane refresh, reducing allowable burst capacity for your workload and triggering 429s.

What we did (already completed):
- Restored tenant override and rolled back the refresh across your deployment (09:12 PT, 10/01).
- Secured trace logs and config snapshots for compliance/audit (request-trace-20261001.zip, config-diff-tenant-vs-app.txt).
- Implemented a hotfix that disables the merging path while we finalize a code fix (deployed 10/02 05:00 PT).

Customer remediation plan:
1) Credits: We'll apply a usage credit equivalent to the requests that returned 429s during the window (we'll reconcile using the trace logs and your CSV) — expected credit posted by 10/05.
2) Short-term safety net: we've provisioned a temporary raised burst ceiling for your tenant for 72 hours while we validate the full fix.
3) Long-term fix: engineering will release a config-merger patch with deterministic reconciliation logic; target release 10/12.
4) Postmortem & controls: full postmortem doc (Drive link below), and we'll add an optional tenant-level safeguard toggle you can enable that forces strict tenant precedence for bursts.

Proposed customer-facing timeline:
- 10/02: Hotfix deployed; 72-hour raised burst ceiling in place.
- 10/05: Credits applied and reconciliation completed.
- 10/12: Code patch released & scheduled for canary; we'll coordinate a canary window with you.

Please let me know if this plan meets your needs or if you'd like a joint call with engineering for the canary.

Drive postmortem: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cPostmortemLink
HubSpot: HS-248392
JIRA: JIRA-INF-5712

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
attachments: config-diff-tenant-vs-app.txt, request-trace-20261001.zip

Subject: Re: Customer recovery plan + timeline (CybeRloom)

Olga — appreciate the clear plan and the fast turnaround. The raised ceiling for 72 hours should be fine; we'll hold off large backfills until the 10/12 canary unless you request otherwise. Please proceed with the credits reconciliation.

Two requests from our side: 
- Please include the final config diff in the postmortem that shows the pre- and post- values (helpful for our auditors).
- Can your SRE join our postmortem sync on 10/13 at 11:00 PT? Aditya or another engineer would be perfect.

Thanks again — Matt
